chunks: From him, from Fadalah, from al-Husayn ibn 'Uthman, from Sama'ah, from Abu Basir, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who prayed two rak'ahs, then stood up and went to relieve himself. He said, 'He faces the direction of prayer.' I said, 'What is the matter with the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) that he did not face the direction when he prayed two rak'ahs?' He said, 'Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did not depart from his place.'
ai.seo_question: What should a person do with their prayer direction if they stand up to relieve themselves after praying two rak'ahs?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the fiqh of *istiqbal al-qibla* (facing the Qibla) during short breaks in prayer, establishing that one must re-face the Qibla if they leave their place, unlike the Prophet who remained stationary. Shaykh al-Tusi includes this in the chapter on *Sahw* (forgetfulness/error) to distinguish between mere movement and actual departure from the prayer spot, a nuance critical for Shia jurists determining the validity of the prayer's continuity. The distinction highlights the Prophet’s unique status and practical example, serving as a foundational precedent for later legal derivations regarding ritual purity and prayer posture.
